## Overview

LRPJM01 turns two quantities the suite currently reports as _sensitivities_ into identified posterior contrasts (#421 Tier 3 (1); letter-sound → word-reading review note #424, decoding-specificity note `202607172358`).

The first is the **conditional-to-marginal slope ratio**: what the letter-sound → word-reading slope becomes when nonword decoding is held fixed, as a fraction of the unconditional slope (0.97 / 0.74 / 0.80 / 0.66 at t1–t4 in the review). That number is currently the ratio of [`ca-011`](../lrp-rli-ca-011/)'s slope to [`ca-010`](../lrp-rli-ca-010/)'s. The second is the **decoding-specificity contrast** Δ = β(LS→N) − β(LS→W), currently paired from [`mech-096`](../lrp-rli-mech-096/) and [`mech-101`](../lrp-rli-mech-101/). In both cases the two fits share children, so the true joint posterior has a cross-outcome covariance that pairing independent draws sets to zero.

This model fits word reading and nonword decoding **together at each wave**, with an **LKJ residual correlation** between them. Both quantities then fall out of one posterior as within-model deterministics.

_This model is not a nested replacement for `ca-010` / `ca-011`._ It is a bivariate logistic-normal Binomial model conditioning on the **latent** held-fixed outcome; the comparators are separate Beta-Binomial fits, and `ca-011` conditions on an **observed** transformed nonword count with missing predictor values mean-imputed. Common rows and a common exposure scale would not make the two nested, so the gap between the two conditional slopes cannot be read as the cost of the working-independence assumption. Read this model as a distinct sensitivity estimand.

_Every published wave is treated the same way._ Each fitted timepoint gets its own persisted trace, its own convergence scan over the deterministics it publishes (not only its free parameters), its own new-child predictive check and its own power-scaling result, and the release decision fails closed if any of that is missing, inconsistent or failed. The wave with the most rows hosts the shared fit-level artefacts; that is an operational choice about file placement and confers no scientific priority, so no result in this report is read off one wave in preference to the others.

## Design

- **Per-wave levels.** One cross-sectional fit per timepoint (`phase_mode="levels"`), one row per child: each outcome's *level* regressed on the standardised same-wave letter-sound logit, with a per-outcome slope. No own baseline — this is a levels model, not an ANCOVA. The phase-stacked ANCOVA parameterisation is [`jm-002`](../lrp-rli-jm-002/)'s job.
- **Matched in construction to the comparators it sits beside.** Adjustment set = age, hearing (`hs` plus its `hs_missing` indicator, per the missing-indicator policy), non-verbal ability (`blocks`) and a flagged group nuisance on the same wide `Normal(0, 1)`, with the same regularising `Normal(0, 0.3)` slope prior as `ca-010` / `ca-011`. That makes the two conditional slopes comparable in construction; it does not make this one a nested replacement for their paired-draws ratio (see the Overview).
- **Prespecified wave minima.** A timepoint is fitted only with at least ten usable children, at least ten observations on **each** outcome and at least ten children observing **both** — the residual correlation and the conditional slope come from jointly observed pairs, which a union count does not bound. A wave below any floor is named and skipped, never silently dropped.
- **LKJ residual correlation.** Both outcomes' residuals come from one bivariate normal, `Σ = diag(σ) Corr diag(σ)` with `Corr ~ LKJ`. This gives outcome-specific residual scales and a free correlation `rho_outcome` — the thing a single shared intercept with a fixed loading of 1 on both logits cannot give, since conditional on such an intercept the two likelihood legs still factorise.
- **Binomial likelihood, deliberately.** The bivariate residual already carries the extra-binomial variance; adding a Beta-Binomial `kappa` would put two overdispersion mechanisms on the same row, which is how the ITT joint's LKJ block became prior-dominated in April 2026. Here the residual *is* the overdispersion, and its correlation is the estimand.
- **Own denominators.** 79 items for word reading, 6 for nonword decoding, never pooled (a flattened-cell likelihood, as in the joint ITT factory).

### The conditional slope

With latent logits `y_k = z β_k + u_k` and `u ~ N(0, Σ)`, conditioning the focal outcome on the other gives

$$\beta(\mathrm{LS} \to W \mid N) = \beta_W - \rho \frac{\sigma_W}{\sigma_N} \beta_N, \qquad \text{ratio} = \frac{\beta(\mathrm{LS} \to W \mid N)}{\beta_W}.$$

That ratio is a **conditional-to-marginal slope ratio, not a bounded pathway share**. It is negative under suppression, above one under amplification, and not summarisable at all as either its denominator or the held-fixed outcome's residual scale `σ_N` approaches zero — that scale divides the conditional slope. One stability rule fixed in advance covers both routes: the posterior must put at least 95% of its mass on each being more than 0.05 logit from zero. Where it fails the ratio is withheld entirely and the denominator-free `abs_slope_reduction` is published in its place; where it holds the ratio comes with the posterior probability of each of the three regions and with no mean. A value below one does not mean part of the association "runs through" decoding: this is an observational model and it identifies no pathway decomposition — a shared unobserved ability moving both slopes together would produce the same ratio.

Note also that this conditions on the **latent** nonword logit where `ca-011` conditions on the *observed* nonword count. Partialling the latent skill is the cleaner reading of "holding decoding fixed". Classical measurement-error intuition suggests it should retain less, but that ordering is not guaranteed across two nonlinear models with different likelihoods, different missing-data handling and floor compression — so the two are **not** presented as bracketing an answer.

### Δ here is a levels contrast, not the Tier-1 one

The Δ this model reports and the Δ in `notes/202607172358-findings-decoding-specificity.md` are **different estimands**, and they need not agree in sign. This one asks how much higher each *score* is per SD of letter sounds; the Tier-1 one asks about each score's post-level given where it started. A shared reading-development / general-ability component lifts the letter-sound → word-reading *level* association without lifting the ANCOVA one, and the 6-item nonword floor compresses nonword levels harder — so a levels Δ can favour word reading while the ANCOVA Δ strongly favours nonword decoding. That is why [`jm-002`](../lrp-rli-jm-002/) exists as a separate model rather than the Tier-1 number being read off this fit.

### One SD is not the same increment at every wave

The letter-sound logit is standardised **within each wave**, so "per SD" denotes a different raw increment at each timepoint (roughly 1.59, 1.38, 1.39 and 1.44 logits at t1–t4 on the current data). The per-wave standard deviations are recorded in `config.json` and disclosed in the results section; read a cross-wave spread of coefficients with that in mind rather than as a spread on one fixed scale.

_Estimand: descriptive association (no causal warrant)._ Every slope is latent-general-ability-confounded — the residual covariance does not stand in for general ability. Δ is a Campbell–Fiske convergent/discriminant argument, **not** identification of a causal decoding effect — and that argument itself assumes a cross-instrument measurement invariance this model does not impose: with unequal loadings on one general ability, the two latent-scale slopes differ even with no causal letter-sound route. Nonword decoding is a 6-item count floored for 72 / 64 / 52 / 40 % of children at t1–t4, so its residual scale — and through it the conditional slope ratio — is the least well determined quantity in the model. The corresponding randomised-arm result is an available-case modified ITT estimate in the ITT suite.

_Missing data._ Outcome missingness is assumed ignorable given the fitted terms, with filled covariates carrying explicit missingness indicators. No missing-not-at-random or complete-case sensitivity is registered: the deferral is deliberate, and its consequence is that every quantity here is conditional on that assumption.
